Wake up for Google Calendar events

AlarmTracker reads the Google Calendar already synced to this phone — no extra login needed.

1. Make sure your Google account's calendar is syncing in Android Settings → Accounts.
2. Tap “Set up” to grant calendar access.
3. Create an alarm, open Schedule and choose Calendar. Set a prep buffer (e.g. 30 min before the first event).

The alarm then follows your schedule automatically: if an event moves the alarm moves, and empty days can be skipped.

A quick guide to every feature
A tour of what AlarmTracker can do.

AlarmTracker checks everything that can silently stop an alarm — exact-alarm permission, notifications, full-screen access (so it rings over the lock screen), alarm volume, battery optimization and Do Not Disturb. Open Settings → Health check anytime to see and fix your status, and the nightly check confirms tomorrow\'s alarm is armed.

To make sure you don\'t sleep through an alarm, it can require a task before it stops: solve math, scan a specific QR code, take a matching photo, or walk a number of steps. If a camera or sensor isn\'t available, the mission safely falls back to math so you\'re never trapped.

Set a default snooze length per alarm. Turn on snooze coaching to make each snooze shorter than the last, and set a weekly snooze budget to cap how often you snooze across all alarms. You can also snooze a ringing alarm with the volume buttons.
Optionally start a silent on-screen sunrise a few minutes before the alarm — the screen gradually brightens from dark to warm to ease you awake before the sound begins.

Instead of a fixed time, an alarm can trigger on a real event. Open an alarm and use “Track an event”: ring when you arrive at a place, when a chosen app posts a notification (like a delivery marked “arrived”), or when a usage limit resets. A guaranteed fallback time always rings even if the signal never comes.

Link outside services under Settings → Connections. Jira is available now — connect with an API token and AlarmTracker sets alarms for issues due soon, checked quietly in the background on your schedule. Google Calendar and more are coming.
The Stats tab scores how well you wake up over time, with charts for wake times and snoozes, an on-time percentage, and a streak. Log your bedtime to enrich the estimate.
After you dismiss an alarm you get a morning report card. If an alarm is ever missed or late, the “Missed alarm reports” screen explains why. A home-screen widget shows your next alarm at a glance.
Everything stays on your device. Export your history to CSV, review what\'s stored, or wipe all data anytime from Settings → Data & privacy.

This permanently deletes all alarms, event history, bedtime signals and settings on this device. This can’t be undone.
Your data stays on this device
AlarmTracker has no account, no sign-in and no servers. Everything — your alarms, wake history and bedtime signals — is stored only in this app on this phone.
Nothing is uploaded. The app makes no network requests to send your data anywhere. There is no analytics or advertising SDK collecting your activity.

The sleep estimate is derived entirely from signals already on your device (your app activity and dismissal times). It never reads health data, usage stats or your location, and it is an estimate of sleep opportunity — not medical sleep tracking.
Sharing is always manual. A report or streak leaves the app only when you tap Share and choose where it goes. You can export a copy of your data as CSV, or wipe everything, at any time from Settings.

Small (100 m) means “practically here”. Large (2 km) gives you a heads-up to start getting ready.
Alerts travel through a relay server. Everything is encrypted on your phone first, so the relay only ever sees scrambled data — it can\'t tell where anyone is.

AlarmTracker is free and always will be — we don\'t charge for this and take no cut.\n\nThe free public relay has rate limits and no uptime guarantee. If you want more, you can buy ntfy Pro from ntfy directly, or self-host ntfy for nothing (it\'s open source). Either way, paste the details under “Change relay”.

Settings → Appearance has three theme choices: Light, Dark, and System default, which follows your phone's own day/night setting. The switch applies instantly — no restart.

Dynamic colour (Android 12+) recolours the app from your wallpaper. Turn it off to use AlarmTracker's own blue palette instead.

Open the sidebar → Friends to pair with someone, then get told when they actually reach — or leave — a place you care about. No more “I'm 2 minutes away”.

Pairing is mutual: you send an invite, they accept. Pairing on its own shares nothing. Each of you separately chooses when to share your location and for how long (30 minutes to 4 hours), it ends by itself, and a notification shows the whole time it's on.

Everything is encrypted on your phone before it's sent, so the relay server can't tell where anyone is. Removing a friend deletes the shared key for good.
